title: On Weak NIZKs, One-Way Functions and Amplification
abstract: An .(Es, E zk)-weak non-interactive zero knowledge (NIZK) argument has soundness error at most .Es and zero-knowledge error at most .E zk. We show that as long as .NP is hard in the worst case, th e existence of an .(Es, E zk)-weak NIZK proofor argument for .NP with .E zk + √ Es < 1 implies the existence of one-way functions. To obtain this result, we introduce and analyze a strong version of universal approximation that may be of independent interest. As an application, we obtain NIZK amplification theorems based on very mild worst-case complexity assumptions. Specifically, [Bitansky-Geier, CRYPTO'24] showed that .(Es, E zk)-weak NIZK proofs (with .Es and .E zk constants such that .Es + E zk < 1) can be amplified to make their errors negligible, but needed to assume the existence of one-way functions. Our results can be used to remove the additional one-way function assumption and obtain NIZK amplification theorems that are (almost) unconditional; only requiring the mild worst-case assumption that if .NP ⊆ ioP/poly, then .NP ⊆ BPP.

Zero-knowledge proofs are a cornerstone of modern cryptography. They allow
a prover to convince a verifier about the validity of an NP statement without
revealing any information about the witness. The fact that nothing is revealed is
captured by demonstrating an efficient simulator that given only the statement,
can simulate a proof that is indistinguishable from a real proof.
